newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower on ringgit weakness.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower on ringgit weakness.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended lower on Tuesday as foreign investors continued to sell down Malaysian shares fearing continued weakness in the ringgit, analysts and dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 3.02 points, or 0.30 percent, lower at 1,012.48. The small-capitalised Second Board index shed 9.26 points, 1.72 percent, to 530.52.

"I've been doing some selling today. The consensus seems to get out of Malaysian shares with large debt, as these could be affected by the ringgit's weakness," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities.

The ringgit touched a 33-month low against the U.S. dollar earlier, slumping to 2.5700 as speculators continued to pound it down. Analysts said the speculators were raising ringgit to sell by selling stocks.
The slump on the Second Board was caused mainly by cash calls on leveraged retail investors hitting the market, said analysts.
"This has been due to margin selling on second liners," said Franklin Tan, vice president of research at brokers Y.K. Fung.
Ekran remained unchanged despite an announcement that its $6.18 billion Bakun dam project may be delayed.

Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said earlier on Tuesday the delay was due to disagreements between Ekran and its main contractor ABB Asea Brown Boveri over the engineering, procurement and construction contract.
Officials at Ekran declined to comment on the news, while ABB officials were not available.
Commerce Asset gained 15 to 6.65 ringgit. Being the lead underwriter of the Bakun project, analysts said any delay in the project would help it to restructure its financing of it.
Tenaga lost 10 cents to 11.00 ringgit in active trading. Analysts said the company's large debt burden may get worse with the weakening ringgit and increasing interest rates.
Malaysia's Consumer Price Index for the year to June 1997 grew by 2.2 percent against 2.5 percent in the same period in 1996. Analysts said the data only had a minimal impact on share prices.
Market volume stood at 244 million shares, valued at 1,743 million ringgit. Losers swamped gainers 500 to 127.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot July contract lost 16 points to 997.1 with 892 lots traded. August futures shed 16.5 points to 999.0 with 28 lots having changed hands.
